messages:
emily.support: FYI opened a support ticket from a customer: they're seeing intermittent HTML pages returned even though they set response_format=structured and Accept: application/json. Happening ~10% of requests over last 24h.

emily.support: Paste from customer repro:

emily.support: ```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  -H "Accept: application/json" \\
  -H "X-Response-Format: structured" \\
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=open-llama-7b

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
{"output": ... }

# but sometimes they get:
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8
<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>
```

sanjay.se: Do we have logs for the failing request IDs? Customer included X-Request-ID: rq_8f2a3b — emily, can you ask for full header dump and timestamps?

emily.support: Already asked, they sent three examples: rq_8f2a3b, rq_8f2a99, rq_8f2b00. Added them to ticket. They say error correlates with spikes in backend latency and with retries from their side which trip billing.

ryan.product: Is this the known HTML fallback path where the edge returns the upstream error page instead of mapping to a structured 5xx JSON response? We had a patch but thought it covered chunked/streaming responses.

infra-bot: @sanjay.se allocated infra trace for rq_8f2a3b -> trace id t-20231207-44b. Upstream service hit timeout at 120s and returned raw HTML. Edge response mapping used default passthrough because header parsing failed.

sanjay.se: Key detail from trace: the upstream returned a 502 with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and a small leading chunk of HTML then connection closed. Our response parser tries to detect JSON by Content-Type first, but if header ordering includes multiple Accepts or malformed accept negotiation, older edge code falls back to passthrough.

emily.support: Customer also reported token rotation earlier that day — they saw a 401 then retried with new token; some retries apparently queued and triggered the same upstream failure path. Billing flagged because SDK retried multiple times.

ryan.product: Two hypotheses: 1) fallback mapping didn't catch chunked HTML body case, still passes HTML through despite client expecting json; 2) Accept header precedence logic at the edge incorrectly picks */* when both are present (some SDKs set Accept: */*, application/json). When we pick */* we don't enforce structured response mapping.

sanjay.se: Repro steps I'll try: 1) send Accept: application/json only 2) send Accept: */*, application/json in that exact order 3) send response_format=structured as header vs query param. Check which combos produce HTML when upstream fails.

emily.support: Customer requested a workaround asap — advised them to add explicit Accept header with single value and to enable exponential backoff to avoid billing spike. They asked if we can guarantee structured JSON fallback for all failures.

ops_oncall: Oncall note: we should ensure fallback mapping happens before header negotiation. I can hotfix a rule to coerce any 5xx upstream into application/json response if request had response_format=structured or X-Response-Format header. Will validate against regressions.

sanjay.se: I'll reproduce locally and attach a unit test. If confirmed, patch will: - prefer response_format header override - treat Accept header list safely (search for explicit application/json token anywhere) - ensure chunked HTML bodies still get generic JSON error wrapper.

ryan.product: Also flag this for billing team — retries + passthrough HTML caused customer's parser to retry and bill more. We should consider a short-term credit and long-term SDK guidance: prefer explicit Accept and idempotency keys to limit retries.

emily.support: Customer update sent: thanks, applying header change and backoff. Asked if we can share ETA for patch.

sanjay.se: ETA for hotfix: ~4 hours for initial rule, then deploy to canary. Full regression + release tomorrow AM. Will post logs and test vectors.

emily.support: Marking ticket as escalated to eng-runtime. I'll update customer after hotfix. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
